Words of Jesus stand inside the tradition at 11:24-11:25; the WEB quotation marks around them neither drive nor corroborate a seam, and they sit inside the row, away from both edges. The participle rp:1Cor.11.24 εὐχαριστήσας is narrative texture inside the tradition, not a thanksgiving frame. At 11:24 the two witnesses differ in the words of institution: RP reads rp:1Cor.11.24 καὶ εἶπεν, Λάβετε, φάγετε· and rp:1Cor.11.24 τὸ ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν κλώμενον·, while SBLGNT reads sbl:1Cor.11.24 καὶ ⸀εἶπεν· Τοῦτό, without the command, and sbl:1Cor.11.24 τὸ ὑπὲρ ⸀ὑμῶν·, without the participle, at signs; the WEB follows the longer wording. Neither reading moves a seam. Further differences inside the span: at 11:23 SBLGNT reads sbl:1Cor.11.23 ᾗ ⸀παρεδίδετο where RP reads rp:1Cor.11.23 ᾗ παρεδίδοτο; at 11:26 SBLGNT reads sbl:1Cor.11.26 ὁσάκις γὰρ ⸀ἐὰν ἐσθίητε, where the other witness reads rp:1Cor.11.26 Ὁσάκις γὰρ ἂν ἐσθίητε; at 11:27 RP reads rp:1Cor.11.27 ἀναξίως τοῦ κυρίου, where the other witness reads sbl:1Cor.11.27 ⸀ἀναξίως,; at 11:29 RP reads rp:1Cor.11.29 τὸ σῶμα τοῦ κυρίου., where the other witness reads sbl:1Cor.11.29 τὸ ⸀σῶμα. Other RP/SBLGNT differences in the span touch no seam (EXTRACTED from the RP/SBLGNT difference list). Divided reading (REPORTED, strategy section 7 C, naming five ways of reading the Eucharist at 11:23-11:34 and giving no content for them): the meal tradition is read in Catholic, Orthodox, Lutheran, Reformed and memorialist ways. Content past that record is ASSUMED: Catholic and Orthodox readers take the body and blood named at 11:24-11:27 as a real presence and the rite as a sacrifice in the sense their churches define; Lutheran readers hold a sacramental union of body and blood with the bread and cup; Reformed readers hold a spiritual presence received by faith; memorialist readers take the words as a memorial, with the line from Zwingli and the setting in many Baptist and free-church communities equally ASSUMED. The phrase about discerning the body at 11:29 is read by some as the eucharistic body and by others as the assembled church (ASSUMED; the holders of the two readings are UNAVAILABLE). These readings are attributed to their holders; the row prefers no reading, and its seams do not depend on which one is held.
